The Employer Identification Number is the federal tax identification number for your organization. It is
required to open a bank account, apply for grants, enter into contracts, and operate as a formal entity. The
online application issues the EIN immediately upon completion. It is free.

mail a confirmation. The number on that page is your EIN.
■ The online application is only available Monday through Friday, 7 AM to 10 PM Eastern Time. If you
attempt it outside those hours it will not be available.

We assigned you an employer identification number (EIN)
Your EIN is 42-2419586. The name control associated with this EIN is THES.
What you need to do
If you did not apply for this EIN, visit IRS.gov/EINNotRequested.
Use this EIN and your name exactly as they appear above when you fill out your tax returns. Otherwise, it may cause delays. 
Keep a copy of this notice for your records because we'll only send it to you once. You can share a copy with future officers of 
your organization or anyone asking for proof of your EIN. If your name or address is incorrect as shown, send the correct 
information to the address at the top of this notice.
What you need to know
When you applied for an EIN, you said your organization is a non-profit. Getting an EIN doesn't mean you're automatically tax-exempt. 
You must apply specifically for tax-exempt status. You can find more information about the application process in Publication 557, TaxExempt Status for Your Organization.
To apply for recognition of tax-exempt status, organizations must complete an application on one of the following forms:
Form 1023, Application for Recognition of Exemption Under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code;
Form 1023-EZ, Streamlined Application for Recognition of Exemption Under Section 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code;
Form 1024, Application for Recognition Under Section 501(a); or
Form 1024-A, Application for Recognition of Exemption Under Section 501(c)(4) of the Internal Revenue Code.
Most organizations claiming tax-exempt status must file a Form 990 series annual information return (Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-PF) or 
notice (Form 990-N) beginning with the year they legally form, even if they have not yet applied for or received recognition of taxexempt status.
If you become tax-exempt, you'll lose that status if you don't file a required return or notice for three years in a row. There are some 
exceptions, but generally, you need to file every year. We start counting those three years from the date we gave you your EIN. If the 
first tax year isn't a full twelve months, you still need to file a return for that year. If your organization didn't legally form in the same tax 
year you received your EIN, contact us.
For the most current information on your filing requirements and other important information, visit IRS.gov/Charities.
Additional Information
Refer to Publication 4557, Safeguarding Taxpayer Data: A Guide for Your Business, for tips on keeping your EIN safe.
Find tax forms or publications by visiting IRS.gov/Forms or by calling 800-TAX-FORM (800-829-3676).

TMI_Founding_Board_ResolutionSigned.pdf
RESOLUTION 6 — APPOINTMENT OF SECRETARY AND TREASURER
RESOLVED, that Rickey Jay Bennett II is hereby appointed to serve additionally as Secretary and
Treasurer of the Institute until such time as additional officers are appointed by the Board, it being
understood that a sole Director may hold multiple offices under the Bylaws of this organization.
RESOLUTION 7 — AUTHORIZATION TO OBTAIN EMPLOYER IDENTIFICATION NUMBER
RESOLVED, that the Minister is hereby authorized and directed to apply for and obtain an Employer
Identification Number (EIN) from the Internal Revenue Service on behalf of The Thessalonian Mandate
Institute, and to execute all forms and certifications necessary to complete such application, including
IRS Form SS-4 or any online equivalent thereof.
RESOLUTION 8 — AUTHORIZATION TO OPEN FINANCIAL ACCOUNTS
RESOLVED, that the Minister is hereby authorized to open one or more bank accounts, credit accounts,
and other financial accounts in the name of The Thessalonian Mandate Institute, to designate
signatories on such accounts, and to execute all documents required by any financial institution in
connection therewith.
RESOLUTION 9 — AUTHORIZATION TO APPLY FOR GRANTS AND GOVERNMENT CONTRACTS
RESOLVED, that the Minister is hereby authorized to identify, apply for, and accept grants, government
contracts, and other funding opportunities on behalf of the Institute in furtherance of its theological
mission, and to execute all applications, agreements, and certifications required in connection therewith.
RESOLUTION 10 — AUTHORIZATION TO HOLD INSURANCE POLICIES AS TREASURY INSTRUMENT
RESOLVED, that the Institute is hereby authorized, consistent with Section 6.3 of the Bylaws, to acquire
and hold one or more whole life insurance policies as an asset of the organization, to use the cash value
thereof as an operating reserve and treasury instrument, and to borrow against such policies in
furtherance of the mission of the Institute, subject to such terms and conditions as the Minister shall
determine to be in the best interest of the Institute.
RESOLUTION 11 — PRINCIPAL OFFICE
RESOLVED, that the principal office of the Institute shall be located in Austin, Travis County, Texas, at
such address as the Minister shall designate, and the Minister is authorized to establish such address
and to maintain or change the same as the needs of the Institute may require.
RESOLUTION 12 — REGISTERED AGENT
RESOLVED, that the Minister is hereby authorized to designate a registered agent for the Institute in the
State of Texas and to take all steps necessary to maintain such designation in compliance with
applicable Texas law.
